text:
incident-bot: PAGER — streaming-service-prod: sudden p95/p99 spike on websocket streams (p99 ~18s). paging oncall. @oncall-sre please ack.

oncall-sre: acked. I'm on. initial glance at SLO dashboard shows a stair-step increase starting ~10:04 UTC. any customer-facing errors?

cs-rep: multiple customers filed transient timeouts and aborted connections. CS ticket 9982 shows client saw partial payload then socket close.

dan: looking at edge traces — chunk timestamps show long gaps between writes on server->client path. gap variance 5-25s. upstream model latency fine. suspect proxy flush or socket buffer stalls.

erin: proxy logs (sanitized) show repeated: `connection write blocked, queued_chunks=120` and frequent `socket_flush timed out after 9s`. also a surge in `socket_write_backpressure` metrics.

frank: noted a recent config change in prod: `proxy.sndbuf_autotune=false` was enabled in last deploy window. I think that forced a lower socket send buffer leading to backpressure when many slow consumers present.

oncall-sre: timeline check — was there a deploy? @eng-proxy-bot what changed 30-90m ago?

eng-proxy-bot: Deploy event: proxy-service v3.6.1 rolled 49m ago. Config changes: `sndbuf_autotune=false`, `writer_threads=2` (was 4), `streaming_chunk_interval_ms=0` left unchanged.

erin: dropping writer threads from 4->2 seems risky under many concurrent streams; writer saturation could cause head-of-line pauses for other connections. combined with smaller send buffers leads to slow flushes.

dan: reproduce locally with a slow-consumer test: open 2k concurrent streams with client ack delay ~8s — saw writer queue depth exceed 10k and many connections stalled.

oncall-sre: mitigation plan options: (A) rollback to writer_threads=4 and enable sndbuf_autotune=true (B) scale proxy-service horizontally (add 30% pods) (C) increase socket timeout thresholds. prefer A + B for quick relief.

frank: rolling config revert to canary (writer_threads=4, sndbuf_autotune=true) — applying to 10% of prod nodes now. monitor.

eng-proxy-bot: config rollout progress: 10% -> 50% in ~4m.

erin: early canary metrics show p99 drop from 18s -> 3.2s on canary nodes. non-canary still high, starting full rollout.

oncall-sre: initiating horizontal scale while rollback rolls: `kubectl scale --replicas=+6 deployment/proxy-service-prod` — adding capacity in parallel.

dan: after full rollout complete p95 ~0.9s, p99 ~1.8s. connection aborts reduced. CS notified.

cs-rep: updated customers in tickets 9982/9987/9991: explained transient issue, mitigation done, support watching.

oncall-sre: root-cause hypothesis: config change reduced proxy write parallelism and disabled OS-level send-buffer autotuning; under a slow-consumer wave this created backpressure that compounded into high tail latency and socket timeouts.

frank: action items immediate: revert config change permanently until we have load-tested this combo; add guarding alert on `queued_chunks > 500` and writer thread saturation; add e2e slow-consumer test to CI.

oncall-sre: longer-term: autoscale policy shim to detect slow-consumer load patterns and pre-emptively scale proxies. also add runbook steps: if p99>5s on streaming endpoints, check writer_threads and sndbuf_autotune quickly.

erin: will open a PR with monitoring alerts and dashboards.

dan: I'll draft a small load-test job for the slow-consumer scenario and add to perf harness.

oncall-sre: assigning postmortem to frank to own writeup and impact calc (SLO burn, affected customers). frank, please include precise timeline, config diffs, and mitigation steps.

frank: taking ownership. will post a preliminary RCA in #postmortems within 8 hours and link the mitigation runbook.

oncall-sre: incident mitigated — keeping 60m watch. thanks everyone for quick response. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED — duration ~39m. alerts cleared.

frank: will follow up with timeline doc and recommended config guardrails. :memo:
